newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bulls still hold sway as IBIS DAX keeps rising.
newsitem.headline: Bulls still hold sway as IBIS DAX keeps rising.

text.p: Upbeat news from across the Atlantic gave German shares a boost early on Friday, with Wall Street closing higher and the continued strength of the dollar keeping the German bull run intact.
By 0714 GMT the IBIS DAX index was up 37.90 points or 0.88 percent at 4,358.42 points.
Dealers were hard pushed to come up with a forecast for the market, though trade was expected to be somewhat quieter.
"No-one knows where this market is going at the moment. It's going up, it's going down, it's pretty unique at the moment and very volatile," a Frankfurt trader said.

The spectre of a possible interest rate rise haunted some market players, after the Bundesbank dropped a subtle hint to the markets that it could swing into action rapidly if a policy change were needed.

The central bank left its M3 target and all of its main interest rates unchanged after its regular policy meeting on Thursday, but kept markets guessing as to where its main money market rate would be set in two weeks' time.
"If an interest rate rise comes, then the DAX is around 500 points too high," one trader said, although another trader said that these fears were exaggerated.

Shares in the news included Siemens AG, which was up four marks or 3.29 percent at 125.50 marks, which traders came after an analysts' meeting on Thursday. They also said that there had been an upgrade by a large investment bank.
The banking sector was again centre of attention, with euphoria over the merger between Hypo-Bank and Vereinsbank still lifting the banks.
First-half results on Thursday also helped underpin sentiment in the sector.
Deutsche Bank was strongly ahead, up 3.11 percent at 124.25 marks.
Dealers said that overall a quiet day was on the cards for the German share market after one of the most turbulent weeks in its history, with resistance pegged at around 4,400 points.
"For next week I expect the market to continue rising," a trader said.
